fix(cv-backend-spec): restore the em dash in the package description

Addresses #169.

## What changes

`packages/cv-backend-spec/package.json`, the `description` field: three JSON escapes, for U+00E2, U+20AC and U+201D (the UTF-8 bytes of U+2014, E2 80 94, read as Windows-1252 and re-escaped, which a JSON reader decodes to three characters instead of one em dash), become a literal U+2014. The description now reads "…shared by jsfeatNext and PureCV — detect, describe, …".

One line, one file. No other change to the manifest: the diff is `1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)`, the file still starts `{` with no BOM, and `JSON.parse` of the description yields exactly one non-ASCII character, U+2014.

## Where it came from

`git log -S` finds the escapes in eed11db (#54, 2026-09-22), the commit that added the package's `exports` map. Before it the line held a literal em dash, so the escape came in with an edit to an unrelated part of the same file. The shape of it (the em dash double-encoded, then re-escaped) is consistent with a read-as-ANSI, write-as-JSON round trip of the kind `CLAUDE.md`'s note on PowerShell already warns against; the commit does not record which tool wrote it.

## Checks

- `npm run check:contract` passes ("every package, pin and lockfile is at 0.5.1").
- `npm run format:check` passes (`package.json` is outside its globs either way).
- A search of the repository's text files for `u00e2`, `u20ac` and the decoded "â€" finds nothing after the change.

## Not in this PR

No changelog line: a package description is not behaviour, and the CHANGELOG asks for a line from a pull request that changes behaviour. Say so if you want one under `[Unreleased]`.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(opencode): fail a turn stuck in a long session.status retry

## What

The OpenCode runner now watches `session.status` for its own session. When OpenCode is retrying and either the retry carries an `action` (a spent quota, e.g. `free_tier_limit`) or the next attempt is more than 10 minutes away (`RETRY_GIVE_UP_MS`), the turn fails with:

`opencode: usage limit reached: <reason> — retry at <ISO>`

`parseUsageLimit` recognizes that message, so the existing usage-limit auto-resume (spec 2026-08-03-auto-resume-after-usage-limit) frees the slot and books a resume for the retry instant. Short transient retries are still ridden out.

## Why

When OpenCode's free tier runs out, it holds the prompt open and retries on its own schedule (here: the next UTC midnight), sending no event in between. An interactive step has no wall clock (`timeoutMs: 0`), and the idle timer only covers parked sessions, so a turn like that had no way out. Four automation runs held `maxParallel` slots for ~11 h and blocked the queue. The shape was confirmed against a live `opencode serve` 1.19.2 (`GET /session/status` → `{type:"retry", action:{reason:"free_tier_limit"}, next:…}`).

## Tests

- New `#retry-limit` / `#retry-soon` scripts in the mock server, plus two tests in `opencode-server-runner.test.ts`. The suite passes 36/36.
- With the fix disabled, the quota test hangs until vitest's timeout (red).

## Backport

`backport release/v0.16.x`: the runner on that line has no `session.status` handling, and `parseUsageLimit` exists there, so the same fix applies.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(git): an open diff follows the repository, and closes once its file is committed

## Problem

Make a change to a file, open its diff, then commit the file. The diff went on showing the change. An open diff kept the before/after contents it read when it opened, and nothing refreshed them. Editing the file again, or staging it somewhere else, left the diff stale in the same way.

## Fix

`DiffOpener` now follows the repository's change lists (staged, unstaged and conflicted). Whenever the status refreshes, each open **working-tree** diff updates:

- **The file still has a change:** the diff reads its contents again. What's on screen stays there until the new contents arrive, so the tab never blanks. If a newer read starts first, the older one is dropped. If the diff has moved to the file's other side in the meantime, the read is dropped too.
- **The whole change is now staged:** the diff moves to the staged side. A file that is only partly staged has a change on both sides; its diff keeps showing the side it was on.
- **The file has no change left** (committed, or put back as it was): the tab closes, the same as Discard already does. Product ruling: close the tab, don't show a "no changes" state.

A commit's diff is history, so it is left alone.

`Diffs` gains `ids()` so the opener can walk the open diffs.

## Tests

- 4 new specs in `diff-opener.spec.ts`: a committed file closes its diff, a re-edited file reloads, a fully staged change moves to the staged side, and a commit's diff is left alone.
- The diffs, diff-document-panel and document-diff-switch specs pass.
- Run locally and passing: `format:check`, `lint`, `build`, `build:electron`.
- The full unit suite is left to CI.
- Tested in the app by the product owner.

fix(windows): make lint, typecheck, build, three test suites and the git hooks run on Windows

Fixes #1397

Four independent reasons a Windows contributor cannot use this repository today, one commit each so you can take or drop them separately. Details, mechanisms and the full before/after numbers are in the issue; the short version:

| Commit | What it fixes | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `fix(scripts)` | root `pnpm lint` fails with **0 of 2 tasks** (`spawnSync drizzle-kit ENOENT`) | resolve `drizzle-kit`'s declared bin entry, launch it with `process.execPath`, fall back to the bare command |
| `build(builder)` | `check-types` and `build` die before doing any work (`cmd.exe` cannot parse a `VAR=value` prefix) | `tsc` through `node` with the heap flag; `dotenv -v SKIP_ENV_CHECK=true`. **No new dependency** |
| `test` | **6 cases** fail in 3 suites comparing a backslash path against a `/` path | normalise both sides to `/`; assertions, allowlists and patterns unchanged |
| `chore(hooks)` | `post-checkout` and `commit-msg` **always** abort, even on valid input | move the two multiline bodies verbatim into `scripts/git-hooks/`, invoke through `sh` |

### How it was verified

Every exit code read directly, not through a pipe. All suites run with `--force`, so nothing came from cache.

**Before, on `e4913ef2a` with no local workaround in place:**

- root `pnpm lint` - exit 2, `Tasks: 0 successful, 2 total`, `Failed: @chatbotx.io/database#lint`
- `pnpm --filter builder check-types` - exit 1, `'NODE_OPTIONS' is not recognized as an internal or external command`
- `worker` suite - 2 files / 5 cases failed (263 files passed)
- `builder` suite - 1 file / 1 case failed (743 files passed)
- `commit-msg` hook with a **valid** message - exit 1, `-c: line 4: syntax error: unexpected end of file`

**After, same machine:**

- root `pnpm lint` - exit 0, `Tasks: 2 successful, 2 total`, and the drift check actually runs: `Schema is in sync with the migration snapshot chain.`
- `pnpm --filter builder check-types` - exit 0, full typecheck completes; `check-types` across the workspace **59 of 59**
- `worker` 265 files / **3198 cases passed** · `builder` 744 files / **5884 passed** (2 skipped) · `chatbotx-mcp` 12 / 178 · `@chatbotx.io/database` 82 / 1108
- hooks: valid message exit 0, invalid message exit 1 with the original help text and `Got: <message>` intact; branch gate exercised on a non-matching name (exit 1), a matching one (exit 0) and `main` (exit 0), in a throwaway repository so the rejection path could be seen without renaming branches here

The two env-shaped fixes were measured with the `script-shell` override removed in **both** passes, so the green is the fix and not a local workaround. The hook scripts are invoked through `sh` rather than relying on the executable bit, which Windows checkouts do not carry.

### Deliberately not included

Two suites have gone over their 5s and 30s budgets in loaded full-suite runs on this machine, but they passed on today's baseline, so there is no reproducible failure to justify changing them and no commit here does.

### Note on #1169

#1169 asks for `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` on six further `check-types` scripts. In the current form that multiplies the `cmd.exe` problem by six; the `node --max-old-space-size=... tsc` form in this PR is portable and puts the flag where it has to be anyway.

fix: the desktop app's Google sign-in (PKCE), plus a demo account and a testing checklist

Bugfix PR for the desktop app; more fixes found while testing go in here too.

**Fix 1: Google sign-in came back with a token in the address bar.** The desktop app's Supabase client was missing \`flowType: 'pkce'\` (an edit in #121 did not apply). Without it Supabase uses the implicit flow and returns the token in the address fragment (\`/auth/desktop#access_token=...\`), which a server page cannot read, so the hand-over to the app could not work. Found by a manual local Google sign-in. Test first (\`tests/unit/data/local/cloud.test.ts\`, failed before the fix).

**Also in this PR (tooling for testing):**
- \`npm run seed:demo\`: a demo account in the LOCAL Supabase (\`demo@cadence.test\`, tag \`@demo\`, a registered profile with a character avatar, three habits with a month of history and focus sessions); \`-- --empty\` for no habits. Refuses anything but a local database.
- \`docs/desktop-testing.md\`: the by-hand checklist for the desktop app.

Unit suite, lint, typecheck pass.
